For Case 1 illustrated in figure 6.3.5.3.1-1, the detailed partiality information is included in messages sent to indicate that enforceStatus is NOT_ENFORCED unless enforceReason is SCOPE_NOT APPLICABLE, while no enforceReason is provided in case the notification only indicates a change in the partiality details (without a change in enforcement status).

For Case 2 illustrated in figure 6.3.5.3.1-2, the detailed partiality information is included in messages sent to indicate that enforceStatus is ENFORCED unless enforceReason is SCOPE_APPLICABLE, while no enforceReason is provided in case the notification only indicates a change in the partiality details (without a change in enforcement status).

For Case 3 illustrated in figure 6.3.5.3.1-3, the detailed partiality information is included in messages sent to indicate that enforceStatus is PARTIALLY_ENFORCED, while no enforceReason is provided in case the notification only indicates a change in the partiality details (without a change in enforcement status).

#### 6.3.5.4 Query partial enforcement status

##### 6.3.5.4.1 Enforcement status related to scope enforceability

For the cases 1 to 3 defined in clause 6.2.3, the detailed partiality information could be provided with the enforcement status in a query response. Depending on the case, the partiality details are only needed when the enforceStatus indicates that enforcement is, or may be, partial.

> NOTE:	In current A1AP [i.3] it is optional to include enforceReason in the query response message, if present it would reflect a situation when the A1 policy is fully enforceable or not enforceable since enforceReason would not be included in notifications with only partiality details.
For Case 1 illustrated in figure 6.3.5.4.1-1, the detailed partiality information would not be needed if the enforceReason indicates SCOPE_NOT_ENFORCEABLE.

For Case 2 illustrated in figure 6.3.5.4.1-2, the detailed partiality information would not be needed if the enforceReason indicates SCOPE_ENFORCEABLE.

For Case 3 illustrated in figure 6.3.5.4.1-3, the detailed partiality information would not be needed if the enforceReason indicates SCOPE_ENFORCEABLE or SCOPE_NOT_ENFORCEABLE.

### 6.3.6 Policy type status changes

#### 6.3.6.1 General

The ability to enforce A1 policies may change, e.g. due to change in the A1 policy enforcement capabilities, and this can be indicated as a change in policy type status (see clauses 6.3.2.5 and 6.3.4.2) as reflected in the opStatus attribute value.

#### 6.3.6.2 Query policy type status

The opStatus attribute would be included in the PolicyTypeStatusObject that may also contain an opReason attribute that reflects the reason for the latest status change.

> NOTE:	Cfr. the inclusion of the enforceStatus and enforceReason attributes in the PolicyStatusObject.

#### 6.3.6.3 Policy type status changes

##### 6.3.6.3.1 General

A change in status of the functionality related to enforcement of A1 policies of a certain type, caused by a change in the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, is reflected as a change in the policy type status (see clause 6.3.2.5). A policy type status change can, but need not, imply a corresponding change in policy status of existing A1 policies of that type while a change in policy status can occur (for other reasons) without any related change to the associated policy type status.

A policy type status change from:

- OPERABLE to INOPERABLE causes a change in policy status for individual A1 policies (of that type) for which enforceStatus = ENFORCED (see note 1):
- OPERABLE to PART_OPERABLE can, but need not, cause a change in policy status for individual A1 policies (see notes 1 and 2); and
- PART_OPERABLE to INOPERABLE can, but need not, cause a change in enforceStatus for individual A1 policies (see notes 1 and 3).
and a policy type status change from:

- INOPERABLE to PART_INOPERABLE can, but need not, cause a change in enforceStatus for individual A1 policies (see notes 1 and 2).
- INOPERABLE to OPERABLE can, but need not, cause a change in enforceStatus for individual A1 policies (see note 1).
- PART_OPERABLE to OPERABLE can, but need not, cause a change in enforceStatus for individual A1 policies (see notes 1 and 4).
- NOTE 1:	If the policy status was NOT_ENFORCED due to other reasons, it would not change when the policy type status changes.
- NOTE 2:	If policy status was ENFORCED, it may remain ENFORCED, or if policy status was NOT_ENFORCED, it may become ENFORCED, if the scope is fully covered by the A1 policy enforcement capabilities available after the policy type status change.
- NOTE 3:	If the policy status was NOT_ENFORCED due that its scope was not fully/partly covered by available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, it would not change when the policy type status becomes INOPERABLE.
- NOTE 4:	If the policy status was ENFORCED due that its scope was fully covered by available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, it would not change when the policy type status becomes OPERABLE.

##### 6.3.6.3.2 Case specific considerations

Policy status and policy type status provide fundamental information for how Non-RT RIC could lifecycle manage an A1 policy by updating it, deleting it, or just waiting for some improvement in the availability of the A1 enforcement capabilities (or resolution of other issues) under assumption that it will improve the achievability of the objectives.

The definition of policy type status is based on A1 policy enforcement capabilities and does not depend on how the enforceStatus attributes values are defined and interpreted (see clause 6.3.5.2). The interpretation of enforceStatus, and policy status changes, depend on the case used for defining the meaning of enforceStatus. The policy status changes may, or may not, be correlated with a change in policy type status.

For Case 1, the policy type status complements the policy status for a specific A1 policy by indicating when the NOT_ENFORCED status could indicate that enforcement actions may be taken for some parts of the A1 policy.

For Case 2, the policy type status complements the policy status for a specific A1 policy by indicating when the ENFORCED status could indicate that enforcement actions are taken for some, rather than all, parts of the A1 policy.

For Case 3, the policy type status complements the policy status for a specific A1 policy by indicating when the policy status may be impacted by the extent to which the policy scope is covered by the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities.

> NOTE:	It is for further consideration what the relevant attribute values for opReason would be, and how they would relate to the enforceReason attribute values.

##### 6.3.6.3.3 Relations between policy type status, policy status, and status changes

Based on definitions and reasoning in clauses 5.5, 6.3.2.5, and 6.3.6.3, figure 6.3.6.3.3-1 illustrates the relation between policy type status and policy status, as well as policy type status changes and policy status changes.

Policy status of an individual A1 policy is based on the enforceability implied by the policy type status but could be impacted by other (dynamic) aspects such as e.g. resource or policy conflicts. Creation of a requested A1 policy is assumed to be based on the (full) applicability and the (full or partial) enforceability of the requested A1 policy, hence policy type status is assumed to be strictly defined based on the availability of configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities. If policy type status is OPERABLE, the requested A1 policy could be accepted (since fully enforceable) or could be rejected (for other reasons); and if policy type status is PART_OPERABLE, the requested A1 policy could be accepted (if fully or partially enforceable) or could be rejected (if not enforceable or for other reasons).

> NOTE 1:	A policy status change (for an A1 policy of a certain type) may be related to a change of the policy type status but may also occur for other reasons (when there is no change in policy type status).
> NOTE 2:	A policy type status change may, or may not, lead to a policy status change for an individual A1 policy.
> NOTE 3: Figure 6.3.6.3.3-1 illustrates Cases 1 and 2 in clause 6.2.3.

## 6.4 Life cycle management and state transitions

### 6.4.1 General

The state diagram in figure 6.4.1-1 reflects the state transitions after the transactions illustrated in figure 5.5.2.2-1 and 5.5.3.2-1 where policy creation is accepted after the enforcement status in known to be ENFORCED.

> NOTE:	This corresponds to figure 4.2.2-1 and is replicated here as basis for further elaborations in the following clauses.

### 6.4.2 Undetermined state

The state diagram in figure 6.4.2-1 reflects the state transitions after the transactions illustrated in figure 5.5.2.3-2 where status is initially UNDETERMINED after policy creation until determined and notified.

> NOTE 1: 	The transaction illustrated in figure 5.5.3.3-1 is similar in the sense that policy creation acceptance can lead to either value of the status.
> NOTE 2: 	It would be for further considerations if status should be reverted to UNDETERMINED during evaluation of a policy update request.

### 6.4.3 Partially enforced state

The state diagram in figure 6.4.3-1 reflects the state transitions after the transactions illustrated in figure 5.5.2.2-1 and 5.5.3.2-1 in Case 3 (see clause 6.2.3).

> NOTE: 	An alternative diagram could include also the UNDETERMINED state.

## 6.5 Summary

The usage of the terms elaborated in clauses 5.3 and 5.4, and in the present clause, can be summarized as:

Requested A1 policy: the policy requested to be created/updated in an A1 policy creation/update request message

Requested scope: the scope in a requested A1 policy

> NOTE 1:	The requested scope may or may not be applicable
Valid A1 policy: a requested A1 policy that validates against the policy schema used by the Near-RT RIC

> NOTE 2:	The Non-RT RIC formulates the A1 policy based on the policy schema before requesting the A1 policy to be created/updated, and the Near-RT RIC will validate the A1 policy against the policy schema when receiving the A1 policy creation/update request. To say the A1 policy validates against the policy schema implies a validation would be successful whenever it is performed and hence the A1 policy is considered as valid.
Accepted A1 policy: a requested A1 policy accepted to be created based on an A1 policy creation/update request message

> NOTE 3:	Term is used instead of saying "created policy" to avoid confusing the outcome of the creation process with the long-term state of the A1 policy representing an enforcement activity
> NOTE 4:	To be acceptable, the requested A1 policy has to be a valid A1 policy and Near-RT RIC may also reject a requested policy that it considers to be in conflict with an existing A1 policy.
Existing A1 policy: an A1 policy created/updated after accepting an A1 policy creation/update request message that has not yet been deleted

> NOTE 5:	Term is used instead of saying "created policy" to avoid confusing the long-term state representing an enforcement activity with the outcome of the creation process
Rejected A1 policy: an A1 policy not accepted to be created/updated based on an A1 policy creation/update request message

> NOTE 6:	The reject reason contained in the A1 policy creation/update response message could be used by the A1-P Consumer to reformulate the requested A1 policy and can currently indicate if the requested A1 policy was considered as “invalid” or "conflicting", and could in future cover other reasons such as e.g. "inapplicable", "unachievable" etc
Applicability: expresses if enforcement of a valid A1 policy can be based on the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities and the supported objective attributes and their supported value ranges

- An A1 policy would be
- "fully applicable" (or simply " applicable ") in case it has a fully applicable scope, the objectives statement is fully applicable, and the resources statement is fully applicable;
- "not applicable" in case it has a not applicable scope, or the objectives statement is not applicable, or no part of the resources statement is applicable; and
- "partly applicable" otherwise
and the objectives statement would be

- "fully applicable" in case all objectives, and the combinations of them, are supported and all attribute values are reasonable;
- "not applicable" in case none of the objectives is supported or none of the attribute values are reasonable; and
- "partly applicable" otherwise.
Applicable scope: the part of the requested scope covered by the configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities

- a "fully applicable scope" is completely covered;
- a "partly applicable scope" is partly covered; and
- a "not applicable scope" has no part covered.
> NOTE 7:	The applicable scope may or may not be enforceable
Enforceable scope: the part of the applicable scope covered by the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities

- a "fully enforceable scope" is completely covered;
- a "partly enforceable scope" is partly covered; and
- a "not enforceable scope" has no part is covered.
Enforceability: expresses if an applicable A1 policy can be enforced based on the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities

- An A1 policy would be
- "fully enforceable" (or simply "enforceable") in case it has a fully enforceable scope, the objectives statement is fully applicable, and the cells in the resources statement are available;
- "not enforceable" in case it has a not enforceable scope, or the objectives statement is not applicable, or no cell in the resources statement is available; and
- "partly enforceable" otherwise.
Enforcement: the activity and actions that strive to achieve the objectives of an existing A1 policy

> NOTE 8:	The A1 interface does not support activation/de-activation of the enforcement of existing A1 policies, an existing A1 policy is always in enforcement
Partial enforcement: the activity and actions that strive to achieve the objectives of an existing A1 policy using a subset of the required A1 policy enforcement capabilities (i.e. enforcement of an A1 policy that is only partly enforceable).

Enforcement status: the status of the enforcement activity as expressed by the enforceStatus attribute

- If the enforceStatus is ENFORCED, enforcement actions are taken for all parts of the A1 policy and the A1 policy is referred to as "fully enforced" (or simply "enforced");
- If the enforceStatus is PARTIALLY_ENFORCED, enforcement actions are taken for some parts of the A1 policy and the A1 policy is referred to as "partially enforced"; and
- If the enforceStatus is NOT_ENFORCED, the A1 policy is referred to as "not enforced".
> NOTE 9:	This describes enforcement status with a dedicated attribute value for handling partiality.
Partial success: the outcome of a create policy transaction where the A1 policy is partially enforced.

# 7 Conclusions and recommendations

## 7.1 General

Updating the A1 interface specification for support of partiality aspects would imply update of several clauses in several of the specifications, and an update of the A1 policy management service (A1-P) may imply a non-backward compatible change.

Clause 7.2 provides a summary of major findings of the study in the present document that could be considered for inclusion in an updated A1 interface specification. Clause 7.3 then provides further details on inclusion of partiality in the definition and interpretation of policy enforcement status.

Clause 7.4 summarizes identified issues and items that were not further considered in the present study.

Clause 7.5 provides the high-level recommendations from the study.

## 7.2 Common aspects

### 7.2.1 Terms

#### 7.2.1.1 General

The partiality discussion in the present document relies on fundamental definitions related to A1 policy enforcement capabilities and to how (the scope, objectives, and resources of) an A1 policy is considered as applicable and enforceable. The reasoning of how partiality can be considered during policy creation and enforcement introduced refined terms for referring to an A1 policy and enforcement as an activity.

The following clause summarizes where the definitions are made.

#### 7.2.1.2 Capabilities

The configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities and the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities defined as in clause 5.3.2 and 6.2.2.

The required A1 policy enforcement capabilities and the available A1 policy enforcement capabilities as discussed in clause 6.1.

#### 7.2.1.3 Abilities

Scope applicability as defined in 6.2.2.

Objectives applicability as defined in 5.3.4 and 6.2.1.

Resources applicability as defined in clause 5.3.5.

Policy applicability and enforceability as defined in clauses 5.4.3 and 6.2.

#### 7.2.1.4 Scopes and policies

Requested/Valid/Accepted/Rejected/Existing A1 policy, and Requested/Applicable/Enforceable scope, as summarized  in clause 6.5.

#### 7.2.1.5 Enforcement

Enforcement as described in clause 5.4.1 and partial enforcement as defined in clause 6.1.

### 7.2.2 Constraints and status

#### 7.2.2.1 General

The definition of policy type constraints and policy type status in clause 6.3.2 would provide detailed information for Non-RT RIC related to what it could expect if a requested A1 policy was formulated in certain ways and in certain contexts so that

- if Non-RT RIC was aware of the policy type specific constraints containing configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities, it would be able to formulate a requested A1 policy with an applicable scope;
- if Non-RT RIC was aware of the policy type specific supported attributes and value ranges, it would be able to formulate a requested A1 policy with applicable objectives;
- if Non-RT RIC was aware of the policy type specific constraints containing available A1 policy enforcement capabilities, it would be able to formulate a requested A1 policy with enforceable scope; and
- if Non-RT RIC was aware of the policy type status, it would be able to realize when the constraints change and reflect status that provides guidance regarding if partial enforcement could be expected for A1 policies.

#### 7.2.2.2 Procedures

Policy type constraints can be provided in the response of a Query policy type constraints operations, or in the response to the Query policy type operation, as discussed in clause 6.3.2.2.

Policy type status can be provided in the response of a Query policy type status operation, or by a Notify policy type status operation, as discussed in clause 6.3.2.5.

#### 7.2.2.3 Schema

Constraints schema and policy type status schema would be part of policy type definitions (together with policy schema and status schema), see clause 6.3.2.

### 7.2.3 Creation/update requests

#### 7.2.3.1 General

The design patterns for how A1 policies can be created and updated using HTTP PUT operations, and the HTTP status codes related to evaluations of policy creation requests, can be applied to support partiality aspects. In addition, the message content could include detailed information that could correspond to information provided in other operations.

#### 7.2.3.2 Create/update policy operations

The Create single policy operations and Update single policy operations are based on HTTP PUT where the requested A1 policy is provided in the message content.

If the requested A1 policy is not considered as applicable, the PUT request could be rejected with a 501 error, and if the requested A1 policy is not considered as enforceable, the PUT request could be rejected with a 503 error, as discussed in clause 5.5.4.2.

> NOTE:	The usage of the error codes 501 and 503 is already allowed, see A1AP [i.3], clause 6.2.7.3, although their relation to A1 policy enforcement capabilities is not covered by the current A1 specification.
The reject message could contain any detailed information on the reject reasons but need not if the corresponding information is provided as policy type constraints and/or status.

#### 7.2.3.3 Design patterns

Evaluation of policy creation requests can be based on only evaluation of applicability/enforceability but can also be based on the status after start of enforcement (when actions are taken for the parts of the policy) as described in clauses 5.5.2 and 5.5.3. Clause 5.5.5 provides potential clarifications to the current A1 specification related to this while clause 6.3.4 elaborates further on how policy creation transactions could be impacted by partiality (depending on cases as described in clause 7.3).

#### 7.2.3.4 Assumptions and expectations

Non-RT RIC can assume that an A1 policy is enforced until policy status is queried or a change in enforcement status is notified while Near-RT RIC can assign any value of enforceStatus when creating the A1 policy before enforcement activity starts and the actual status may be notified. To avoid risk for situations where the assumptions may leave Non-RT RIC unaware of the actual status of the enforcement activity, the proposed clarification (see clause 5.5.5) is that the Non-RT RIC should query the policy status after receiving the 201 Created as that enables understanding of the policy status in both cases when a policy status notification is either received or not.

### 7.2.4 Status and notifications

The change reason attributes values in the policy status notifications can reflect partiality information. In addition, the message content could include detailed status information that could correspond to information provided in other operations.

Potential updates of enforceReason attributes values are discussed in clause 6.2.4 and detailed policy status information in clause 6.2.5. Clause 5.5.5 provides potential clarifications to the current A1 specification related to this while clause 6.3.5 elaborates further on how policy creation transactions could be impacted by partiality (depending on cases as described in clause 7.3).

## 7.3 Defining and interpreting enforceStatus

### 7.3.1 General

The definitions referred to in clause 7.2 can be applied to support partiality irrespective of if/how the enforceStatus attribute values are defined and interpreted as they reflect policy type and enforcement capability related properties rather than properties of any individual A1 policy.

The enforcement status is specific for an individual A1 policy. The detailed change information of the policy status and the policy type status identified in the present document refers to the same attributes as those related to the A1 policy enforcement capabilities of the A1 policy type.

### 7.3.2 Lifecycle management

The current description of A1 policy lifecycle management in A1GAP [i.1], clause 5.1.3, would be impacted by clarifications/updates related to the policy creation transactions (see clause 7.2.3) and to definitions/interpretations of policy enforcement status.

> NOTE:	The present document does not consider any changes to the principle that Non-RT RIC is the lifecycle management owner of A1 polices while Near-RT RIC determines the status of the A1 policy enforcement activities for existing policies.

### 7.3.3 Reinterpreting the current case

Case 0 introduced in clause 6.2.3 corresponds to the current A1 specification. By introducing supporting information as per clause 7.2, the current definitions of the enforceStatus attributes values can be kept if interpretations (and Non-RT RIC assumptions) are clarified as:

- if requested A1 policy is not applicable (i.e. it is not "fully applicable"), the policy creation request can be rejected using the 501 error code;
- if requested A1 policy is not enforceable (i.e. it is "fully enforceable" or "partly enforceable"), the policy creation request can be rejected using the 503 error code;
- if the requested A1 policy is accepted using the 201 response code, Non-RT RIC can assume Near-RT RIC considers it as enforceable and will start an enforcement activity.
Non-RT RIC would be expected to query policy status (when needed) to get guidance on if observable impact of the A1 policy can be expected, and if to consider keeping/updating/deleting the A1 policy. The enforceReason attribute values, and any detailed policy status information, would enable Near-RT RIC to express detailed partiality information. Policy status notifications could indicate changes in the detailed policy status information as well as changes in enforceStatus attribute value.

The policy type constraints and status would provide guidance to Non-RT RIC regarding what can be an expected outcome of a policy creation transaction. The policy type status would indicate if full or partial enforcement could be expected based on configured A1 policy enforcement capabilities being completely or partly available, and the policy type constraints would provide detailed information on available A1 policy enforcement capabilities.

> NOTE:	Even if the same attributes (providing information on availability of A1 policy enforcement capabilities) are used to indicate status of policy types as to indicate status of an individual policy, the policy type status does not reflect status of an individual policy.

### 7.3.4 New alternative definitions

#### 7.3.4.1 Case 1

Case 1 introduced in clause 6.2.3 implies stricter expectations, compared to case 0 described in clause 7.3.2, regarding Near-RT RIC behaviour and implies Non-RT RIC can assume:

- enforceStatus = ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce all parts of the A1 policy; and
- enforceStatus = NOT_ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce some parts, or no part, of the A1 policy.
It also implies stricter relations between the enforceStatus and enforceReason values as described in 6.3.5.3.1.

#### 7.3.4.2 Case 2

Case 2 introduced in clause 6.2.3 implies stricter expectations, compared to case 0 described in clause 7.3.2, regarding Near-RT RIC behaviour and implies Non-RT RIC can assume:

- enforceStatus = ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce all parts, or some parts, of the A1 policy; and
- enforceStatus = NOT_ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce no part, of the A1 policy.
It also implies stricter relations between the enforceStatus and enforceReason values as described in 6.3.5.3.1.

#### 7.3.4.3 Case 3

Case 3 introduced in clause 6.2.3 introduces an additional attribute value specifically for partial enforcement and implies stricter expectations, compared to case 0 described in clause 7.3.2, regarding Near-RT RIC behaviour and implies Non-RT RIC can assume:

- enforceStatus = ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce all parts of the A1 policy;
- enforceStatus = PARTIALLY_ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce some parts of the A1 policy; and
- enforceStatus = NOT_ENFORCED means enforcement actions are taken to enforce  no part of the A1 policy.
It also implies stricter relations between the enforceStatus and enforceReason values as described in 6.3.5.3.1 and an update to the lifecycle management state transition diagram.

## 7.4 Inconclusive items

### 7.4.1 Effect of enforcement

The present document does not cover aspects related to feasible of being aware of the connected state of all targeted UEs, and if there would be any reason to notify such changes, as discussed in clause 5.4.2.

### 7.4.2 ACID properties for partiality

The present document does not cover any impact on how ACID properties are defined and analysed, after introduction of partiality-related definitions and features, as discussed in clause 5.5.4.

### 7.4.3 Partial content

Usage of the HTTP status code 206 Partial Content was not considered in the present study, as noted in clause 6.3.4.3, since it would imply a significant change to the principles for A1 policy lifecycle management.

## 7.5 Recommendations

### 7.5.1 General

If updates to the A1 interface specification for support of partiality aspects are to be done, they should be based on a work item that enables coordination and alignment of CRs that could be approved for the same O-RAN train release and ensure there is only a minimum number of non-backward compatible API changes.

In such work item, it should be described what approaches and options identified in the present document that should be the basis for the specification update in case the scope is larger than the specific recommendations in clause 7.5.2.

### 7.5.2 Specific

#### 7.5.2.1 Capabilities and abilities

The A1 specification should define terms related to applicability, enforceability, and A1 policy enforcement capabilities to enable inclusion of partiality aspects.

See further clauses 7.2.1.2 and 7.2.1.3.

#### 7.5.2.2 Rejection of not applicable policy

The A1 specification should define usage of the 501 Not Implemented error code for the case when a policy creation request is rejected due to that the requested A1 policy is not considered as "fully applicable".

See further clauses 7.2.3.2 and 7.3.3.

#### 7.5.2.3 Rejection of not enforceable policy

The A1 specification should define usage of the 503 Service Unavailable error code for the case when a policy creation request is rejected due to that the requested A1 policy is considered as "not enforceable".

See further clauses 7.2.3.2 and 7.3.3.

#### 7.5.2.4 enforceReason attribute values

The A1 specification should be updated with enforceReason attribute values SCOPE_NOT_ENFORCEABLE and SCOPE_PARTLY_ENFORCEABLE, and the current values for SCOPE_NOT_APPLICABLE should be clarified to enable status change notification related to loss of A1 policy enforcement capabilities.

The A1 specification should be updated with enforceReason attribute values SCOPE_APPLICABLE and SCOPE_ENFORCEABLE to enable status change notification related to recovery of A1 policy enforcement capabilities.

See further clause 7.2.4.

#### 7.5.2.5 Query policy status

The A1 specification should recommend Non-RT RIC to query policy status when receiving a 201 Created after making a policy creation request to avoid taking actions on assumptions related to Near-RT RIC behaviour.

See further clause 7.2.3.4.

#### 7.5.2.6 Policy type status

The A1 specification should be updated with definitions of policy type status with attribute values that enable indication of that the policy enforcement functionality is OPERABLE (i.e. all the configured A1 enforcement capabilities are available), PART_OPERABLE (i.e. some of the configured A1 enforcement capabilities are available), or INOPERABLE (i.e. none of the configured A1 enforcement capabilities are available).

See further clauses 7.2.2.1, 7.2.2.2, and 7.3.3.

#### 7.5.2.7 Policy type constraints

The A1 specification should be updated with definitions for policy type constraints that enable indication of which configured A1 enforcement capabilities that are available.

See further clauses 7.2.2.1, 7.2.2.2, and 7.3.3.

# 3 Definition of terms, symbols and abbreviations

## 3.1 Terms
For the purposes of the present document, the terms apply: A1-EI: A1 Enrichment Information A1-P: A1 Policy A1-ML: A1 Model management CM: Configuration management FM: Fault management FOCOM: Federated O-Cloud Orchestration and Management NFO: Network Functions Orchestration Non-RT RIC: Non-Real Time RIC PM: Performance management SMO: Service Management and Orchestration SMOS: SMO service

## 3.2 Symbols
Void.

## 3.3 Abbreviations
Void.

# 4 Impact analysis of Decoupled SMO

## 4.1 WG2 specifications impact analysis

### 4.1.1 Non-RT RIC architecture related aspects

#### 4.1.1.1 Overview and highlights
The architecture defined in Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] provide a functional description of Non-RT RIC and SMO, where reference to SMO functions is given in support of the services exposed over the two open interfaces, i.e. R1 and A1.

#### 4.1.1.2 Impact analysis

##### 4.1.1.2.1 Introduction
In the Decoupled SMO FWID, the standardization of a Service Based Architecture for SMO, as defined in OAD [i.2] aims at ensuring the interoperability between components based on the definition of services instead of functions and interfaces. The new approach, however, does neither change the role of the Non-RT RIC nor introduce non-backward compatibility issues over R1 and A1, being the functions defined in the current Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] are one-to-one related to the corresponding services, which can now be referred to a SMOS in OAD [i.2]. Both Decoupled SMO Architecture TR [i.1] and OAD [i.2] state that grouping of SMOS producers in one SMOF is not subject to specification. Moreover, current Non-RT RIC architecture, shows O1, O2 and Open FH M-Plane interface terminations as distinct functions from the functions providing services to Non-RT RIC. With the introduction Decoupled SMO architecture, as described in OAD [i.2] the O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interface terminate to RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM SMOS producers, respectively. Hence, Figure 6.1-1 and the definitions of interface terminations should be revised accordingly.

##### 4.1.1.2.2 Conclusions
Based on the above analysis, the following can be concluded:
- Non-RT RIC architecture remains consistent with the overarching Decoupled SMO architecture, improving
interoperability and enabling a modular approach to service management.
- SMOS (SMO Services) concept should be integrated into the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] to ensure it
aligns with the Service-Based Architecture (SBA) principles of the Decoupled SMO framework.
- Description of O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interfaces and the related services should be adapted to the align with the
Decoupled SMO architecture and principles, e.g. by removing the interface termination boxes and refer to the corresponding SMOS producers (RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM).

### 4.1.2 A1 related aspects

#### 4.1.2.1 Overview and highlights
In the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3], A1 termination function which is anchored function in the Non-RT RIC reference architecture is defined as, A1 termination: It enables the Non-RT RIC framework and the Near-RT RIC to exchange messages over the A1 interface. However, In the Decoupled SMO Architecture TR [i.1] A1 termination function is neither mentioned nor shown in Fig 6.2.1-1. It's not clear then whether it is consistent with the Non-RT RIC Architecture.

#### 4.1.2.2 Impact analysis

##### 4.1.2.2.1 Introduction
A1 Policy, A1 Enrichment Information and A1-ML Model management (A1-P, A1-EI, A1-ML) services are critical for facilitating interaction between the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework and Near-RT RIC through the A1 interface. The management of policies, enrichment information and ML model ensures that near real-time decisions made at the Near-RT RIC are guided or assisted by the management and orchestration services in the SMO/Non-RT RIC. However, there is currently ambiguity about whether producers of these services should be anchored within the Non-RT RIC or be non-anchored (i.e. flexibly deployable as part of the SMO framework or the NonRT RIC framework). The introduction of A1 related SMOSs with the exposure of services offered by a function consuming A1 interface services, i.e. A1-P, A1-EI and A1-ML in A1GAP [i.4], does not conflict with the A1 interface specifications and with the role of Non- RT RIC, There is however an inconsistency related to the concept of “A1 termination" anchoring, introduced in Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3]. As for SMOS related to other external SMO interfaces, i.e. O1 and O2, it would be straightforward to assume that the A1- related SMOS producer and the termination of A1 interface are tightly coupled. The alternative, i.e. introducing a functional separation between the A1 related SMOS producer and the A1 interface termination, would require the definition of an additional interface or reference point between these to ensure interoperability between the two functions. Before the introduction of SMOS concept, the only consumers of A1 related services were the rApps. With the introduction of other SMOS, e.g. Service Assurance SMOS, also other SMOS producer may consume A1 related services SMOS to e.g. provide policies to Near RT RIC. For this reason, it seems appropriate to expose A1 related services as individual SMOS, as defined in OAD [i.2] Following the analysis given above, in order to confirm the assumption that A1 related functions are not anchored to the Non- RT RIC, it is necessary to revise the concept of A1 termination, possibly aligning to other SMO interfaces like O1 and O2, for example avoiding the term “A1 termination function” and use “A1 interface" or “A1 services consumer/producer” instead.

##### 4.1.2.2.2 Conclusions
Based on the above analysis, the following can be concluded:
- Update the descriptions of “A1 termination” in Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3], remove the box “A1
termination" from the Non-RT RIC architecture and terminate the A1 interface into the “A1 related functions”. Remove the reference to "A1 termination" from clause 8.1 and replace the remaining two occurrences of "A1 termination" with "A1 interface. This will ensure consistency between the concepts “A1 related SMOS” given in OAD and the “A1 related functions” described in Non-RT RIC Architecture TS.

### 4.1.3 R1 related aspects

#### 4.1.3.1 Overview and highlights
The standardization of a Service Based Architecture for SMO, as defined in OAD [i.2] aims at ensuring the interoperability between components based on the definition of services. Several SMOS were introduced in OAD [i.2] clause 5.3.1.2.1 to support a service-based architecture in SMO. In particular, the scope of SME and DME SMOS have been defined to support service and data exposure to both internal and external SMOS consumers: SME SMOS supports the exposure of other SMOSs, to both internal and external SMOS consumers. DME SMOS supports the exposure of data produced by SMOS Producers, to both internal and external SMOS consumers. The R1 interface related specifications refer to the services exposed as “R1 services”, since the scope is the service exposure over R1 interface. The relationship between R1 services, SMOS and R1 interface has been provided in OAD [i.2]: R1 Services: The SMOS capabilities available for consumption by rApps, and the capabilities produced by rApps, that are accessible via the R1 interface

#### 4.1.3.2 Impact Analysis

##### 4.1.3.2.1 R1 Interface
The following paragraphs describe the R1 interface (Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] clause 6.2): The R1 interface is a service-based interface via which the R1 services can be consumed and produced. The R1 termination enables the R1 Service Producers and R1 Service Consumers to exchange messages via the R1 interface. The R1 termination enables the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework and the rApps to exchange messages via the R1 interface, assuming that the R1 service APIs and the rApps are registered with the R1 service management and exposure functions. The R1 interface is clearly identified between SMO/Non-RT RIC Framework and the rApps. This is not changed by the Decoupled SMO Architecture.

##### 4.1.3.2.2 R1 services
The following paragraphs describe “R1 services” concepts. From Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] clause 6.2: The R1 services are a collection of services produced and consumed by logical functions in the SMO/Non-RT RIC framework or by rApps. The invoker of an R1 service is referred to as R1 Service Consumer and the provider of an R1 service is referred to as R1 Service Producer. R1 Service Consumers can be rApps and/or SMO/Non-RT RIC framework functions. Further, R1 Service Producers can be rApps and/or SMO/Non-RT RIC framework functions. An rApp as well as a SMO/Non-RT RIC framework function can produce zero or more R1 Services, likewise an rApp as well as a SMO/Non-RT RIC framework function can consume zero or more R1 Services. From Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] clause 7.1: The set of R1 services which can be accessed via the R1 interface includes (but is not limited to):
- Service management and exposure services, which include service registration and service discovery services,
authentication services, authorization services and communication support services. The service management and exposure services support extensibility of the set of R1 services.
- Data management and exposure services, which deliver data created or collected by Data Producers to Data
Consumers according to their needs.
- A1-related services, which provide access to functionality related to A1.
- AI/ML workflow services, which provide access to AI and ML workflow.
- RAN OAM-related services, which provide access to RAN OAM functionality related to the O1 and open
fronthaul M-plane interfaces, and to the OAM functionality related to RAN-specific network slicing in the SMO framework.
- O2-related services, which provide access to functionality related to O2.
- rApp management services, which provide functionality for managing rApps.
- TE&IV-related services, which provide access to topology and inventory data.

##### 4.1.3.2.3 Conclusions
From the above, the following considerations can be derived:
- R1 services and SMOSs listed in OAD [i.2] clause 5.3.1.2.1 and in Non-RT RIC Architecture specification
- SMOSs capabilities can be consumed/produced by rApps via R1 interface
- the introduction of Decoupled SMO architecture does not conflict with the R1 interface principles listed in
R1GAP [i.5] clause 4.2
- The R1AP [i.6] defines a service-based interface. The procedures can be extended to align with the Decoupled
SMO principles without major changes to the APIs.

### 4.1.4 Use cases and requirement related aspects

#### 4.1.4.1 Overview and highlights
WG2 Use cases and requirements so far assume a functional architecture for SMO. The Decoupled SMO feature relies on a Service Based Architecture for SMO and introduces the concepts of SMOS producers/consumers.

#### 4.1.4.2 Impact analysis

##### 4.1.4.2.1 Use cases
Some of the use cases in UCR [i.8] describe the procedures involving SMO components as considering the functional architecture of SMO. The introduction of a service-based architecture for SMO, implies that the SMO functional entities, and the related blocks in the diagrams, should be analysed and aligned to the corresponding SMO service producers/consumers (as an example, ‘RAN NF OAM SMOS producer’ instead of ‘Collection & Control’ in Fig. 4.1.3.1-1).

##### 4.1.4.2.2 Requirements
Clause 5 of UCR [i.8] specify Non-RT RIC, A1 and R1 functional and non-functional requirements. Terminology may need a revision to align to Decoupled SMO architectural principles and definitions.

##### 4.1.4.2.3 Conclusions
UCR [i.8] should be analysed and aligned to comply with Decoupled SMO Architectural principles.

## 4.2 Recommendations
The following actions are recommended to ensure alignment of WG2 specifications for the introduction of the Decoupled SMO Architecture:
- Introduce SMOS (SMO Services) concept into the Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] to ensure it aligns with
the Service-Based Architecture (SBA) principles of the Decoupled SMO framework and the definition of R1 services.
- Analyze and align description of O1/Open FH M-Plane and O2 interfaces and the related services in Non-RT RIC
Architecture specification [i.3] to comply with Decoupled SMO Architectural principles, e.g. by removing the interface termination boxes and refer to the corresponding SMOS producers (RAN NF OAM and NFO/FOCOM).
- Remove the box “A1 termination" from the Non-RT RIC architecture and terminate the A1 interface into the “A1 related
functions”.
- Remove the reference to "A1 termination" from clause 8.1 of Non-RT RIC Architecture specification [i.3] and replace
the remaining two occurrences of "A1 termination" with "A1 interface.
- Analyse and align UCR [i.8] to comply with Decoupled SMO Architectural principles.

# 3 Definition of terms, symbols and abbreviations

## 3.1 Terms

For the purposes of the present document, the following terms apply:

E2SM: E2 Service Model

Near-RT RIC: Near-Real Time RIC

Non-RT RIC: Non-Real Time RIC

## 3.2 Symbols

Void

## 3.3 Abbreviations

For the purposes of the present document, the following abbreviations apply:

PAET: A1 policy applicable entity type

# 4 Overview

## 4.1 Background

Within O-RAN, A1 Policies and E2SMs [i.5] IE/Objects enable the intelligent guidance of the RAN towards better fulfilment of the RAN Intent. Non-RT RIC and Near-RT RIC, each has its own context that need to be broken down into more detailed ones and to be passed to next lower layer as shown in Figure 4.1-1.

> NOTE:	The RAN intent is outside the scope of the A1 interface.
The purpose of the A1 policies is to guide the RAN towards the overall goal expressed in RAN intent in A1GAP [i.1]. As the service consumer of A1 policy management services, rApps can send A1 policies based on their own business purpose, and A1 policy conflict may happen there. Non-RT-RIC-ARCH [i.2] has defined conflict mitigation for A1 policies as follows: If more than one policy generation rApps set contradicting A1 policy statements to the same or overlapping policy scope identifiers, A1 policy function decides to reject the creation/modification request of one or more A1 policies or to temporarily suspend the enforcement of one or more A1 policies.

## 4.2 Concept

### 4.2.1 A1 policy conflict

#### 4.2.1.1 Definition

A1 policy conflict: A situation where it is not feasible for a Near-RT RIC function, and hence the RAN to apply the guidance provided by a set of two or more A1 policies to concurrently achieve the policy objectives and/or to satisfy the conditions for policy resource usage.

#### 4.2.1.2 General description

A1 policy conflict would be generally recognized in two ways; “actual conflict” and “potential conflict”. The actual A1 policy conflict would be detected and handled for created A1 policies at a Near-RT RIC while the potential A1 policy conflict would be predicted and mitigated for requested A1 policies over R1 interface at the Non-RT RIC before a new A1 policy is requested to be created or an existing policy at a Near-RT RIC is requested to be updated over A1 interface.

The potential A1 policy conflict would be predicted by analysing contents of a requested policy and existing policies to be concurrently enforced at a Near-RT RIC, and mitigated to avoid the policy conflict with possible approaches of resolutions.

This TR will study and describe ways to predict and mitigate potential A1 policy conflicts in Non-RT RIC, and this involves further study of A1 policy conflict mitigation functionality of A1 policy functions as specified in Non-RT-RIC-ARCH [i.2], clause 8.4.1.

> NOTE:	The potential A1 policy conflict is referred to as the A1 policy conflict or just the policy conflict, and the usage of term “predict” for policy conflict does not preclude the usage of term “detect” for policy conflict if not necessary to distinguish between them in the Technical Report.

# 5 Use cases

## 5.1 Use case #1 “reserve policy” vs. “release policy”

### 5.1.1 Description

Policies of different A1 policy types currently defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 7.2 could be conflicting with policy objectives and policy resources. Policies of different types with policy objectives (possibly with policy resources) such as QoS/QoE target, QoS/QoE optimization with resource directive, UE level target, Slice SLA target, Load balancing, Energy savings could be conflicting to achieve their objectives concurrently. Policies of the TSP type with policy resources such as Traffic steering preferences could be conflicting to satisfy the conditions for resource usage for the policy concurrently.

It is assumed that one of ways to categorize policy types is into mutually exclusive groups in terms of effect on RAN resource: “reserve policy” group and “release policy” group. The “reserve policy” group is for guaranteeing the service quality possibly by reserving resources, and the “release policy” group is for offloading cells and hence releasing the reserved resources. A general grouping of A1 policy types with clause numbers of A1TD [i.4], clause 7 into these groups is illustrated in Figure 5.1.1-1.

> NOTE 1:	A Traffic steering preferences policy is allowed to have both a cell list of SHALL/PREFER preference and a cell list of AVOID/FORBID preference. In this case the policy would have both characteristics of reserve policy and release policy groups with each specified scope.
> NOTE 2:	A Load balancing policy would have characteristic of reserve policy with traffic increase effect on specified cells and of release policy with traffic decrease effect on other specified cells in the middle of fulfilling the policy. At the stable condition brought by the LB policy there remains characteristic of reserve policy for both specified cells.
> NOTE 3:	An Energy savings policy would imply the coordination with appropriate traffic steering not to impair the user experience, and a policy without esObjectives would not be conflicting with reserve policy group resulting in best effort behaviour for energy savings. With esResource statement along with AVOID/FORBID, the possible energy saving schemes would be more strictly limited for specified cells, but it leaves to the Near-RT RIC whether it can perform the energy saving scheme (e.g. ASM) so as not to give impact on traffic or cell coverage as described in AITD [i.4] clause 6.3.4.5.
Co-existence of these different groups of A1 policies in a Near-RT RIC would have a conflicting situation for achieving their objectives.

### 5.1.2 Some representative scenarios

Service-guaranteed vs. Network energy saving without EsResource.

Service-guaranteed policies (QoS/QoE/UE-level/Slice_SLA) guide to reserve RAN resources while NES without EsResource policies to release the same reserved RAN resources to expand its potential power-off duration.

Load balancing vs. Traffic steering preference with AVOID/FORBID

LB policies guide to reserve RAN resources at the target cells listed in the LbResources for distributing traffic load while TS preference policies to release the same reserved RAN resources at the target cells listed in the TspResources with AVOID/FORBID.

Traffic steering preference with SHALL/PREFER vs. Network energy saving without EsResource.

TS preference policies guide to reserve RAN resources at the target cells listed in the TspResources with SHALL/PREFER while NES without EsResource policies to release the same reserved RAN resources.

## 5.2 Use case #2 Policy objectives not uniquely identified.

### 5.2.1 Description

Entities in subset/intersection set relation of two or more different policies scopes in a Near-RT RIC would have a conflicting situation for identifying an unique policy objectives.

### 5.2.2 Some representative scenarios

UE-level vs. Slice SLA policies

In case that UE-level policy (ex. UL/DL RAN UE Throughput) and Slice SLA policy (ex. Max UL/DL Throughput per UE) specify the same entity in their scopes, it’s not clear which of policies to be applied for that entity as illustrated in Figure 5.2.1-1.

QoS target vs. Slice SLA policies

In case that QoS target policy (ex. UL/DL Guaranteed Flow Bit Rate) specifies a QoS flow in its scope that is impacted by a Slice SLA policy (ex. Max UL/DL Throughput per UE), it’s not clear which of policies to be applied for the QoS flow as illustrated in Figure 5.2.1-2.

## 5.3 Use case #3 Policy resources preference not uniquely identified.

### 5.3.1 Description

Especially for the Traffic steering policy, UEs which are commonly specified with different “SHALL” preferences by different Traffic steering policies would have a conflicting situation for identifying a unique policy resources preference.

### 5.3.2 Some representative scenarios

TSP policy with ueId specified vs. TSP policy with qosId specified for different “SHALL” preference cells.

In case that there are two different TS policies; one for specified UE with {SHALL}={Cell-B} for optimizing UE performance and the other for specified QoS with {SHALL}={Cell-C} for optimizing QoS performance, UEs specified by TSP policy with ueId would have a conflicting situation for identifying a policy resources preference as illustrated in Figure 5.3.2-1 if conditions shown below are met.

- There can only be a conflict in case UEs for which policy#1 is applied has a session established for the qosId covered by policy#2.
- There can only be a conflict when the UEs are connected to cells that have a neighbourhood relation to the cells in cellList of policy 1 (cell-B) and the cells in cellList of policy#2 (cell-C).
- There can only be a conflict in case the cellLists with SHALL preference are disjoint.

# 6 Detection of A1 policy conflict

## 6.1 General

The detection of A1 policy conflict would be performed when a new policy is requested to be created against a set of existing policies, or an existing policy is requested to be updated within a set of existing policies. The decision to regard a set of policies as a set of conflicting policies would be performed based on the following aspects:

to detect if there are overlapping scopes with their policy scopes or overlapping resources in their policy resources, and

to detect if A1 policies in each overlapping scope have potential conflict.

An example flowchart of A1 policy conflict detection is shown in Figure 6.1-1.

## 6.2 Detection of overlaps with policy scope and policy resource

Some examples of the overlapping scope with two policy scopes are illustrated in Figure 4.2.2.1-2. An example on top of the referred figure is a case of subset/superset relation with their policy scopes where scope of policy#1 is subset of scope of policy#2 or scope of policy#2 is superset of scope of policy#1. An example on bottom of the referred figure is a case of joint sets relation with their policy scopes where both scopes of policy#1 and policy#2 are joint sets having an intersection.

### 6.2.1 A1 policy applicable entity type

The ScopeIdentifier in an A1 policy contains the attributes (ueId, groupId, sliceId, qosId, cellId, cellIdList and talList) defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 6.3.1.1, and also the policy statement contains the policy resources (TspResources, SliceSlaResources, LbResources, EsResource) defined in A1TD [i.4], clause 6.3.4 which include identification of policy resources with the attributes commonly used by the ScopeIdentifier (e.g., cellIdList in TspResource, cellIdList/taIList in SliceSlaResources, cellIdList in LbResources, cellIdList in EsResource).

Applicable entity is an entity which is derived explicitly or implicitly by policy scope, relevant granularity level of O1 observables corresponding to the policy objectives, and possibly by policy resources in a policy for identifying overlapping scope or overlapping resource between policies. An A1 policy would have at least one applicable entity type by policy scope and another applicable entity type possibly by policy resource. Based on the A1TD [i.4], clause 7.2, there are several types of A1 policy applicable entity to be derived from allowed combinations of attributes in ScopeIdentifier for policy types: explicit UE, implicit UE(s), explicit Slice and explicit Cell as shown in Table 4.2.2.2-1. As for A1 policy applicable entity derived by policy resource, there is only one type of explicit Cell.
